source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Clinician and client exchange evidence, risks, benefits, values, and goals and work toward a shared decision","B":"Clinician makes the decision alone and avoids discussing reasonable alternatives with the client","C":"Client receives no clinical guidance and must choose entirely alone among unfamiliar treatment options","D":"Process is appropriate only when exactly one treatment option exists and no preference is involved"}}
source_row.rationale: AHRQ defines shared decision making as a collaborative process in which patients and clinicians make decisions informed by evidence, clinician knowledge and experience, and the patient's values, goals, preferences, and circumstances.
source_row.source_detail: Current AHRQ definition: collaborative process involving evidence, care-team knowledge/experience, and patient values, goals, preferences and circumstances.
source_row.stem: A client and clinician are choosing among several reasonable treatments. What best describes shared decision making?
